newsitem.title: JAPAN: Interest rate change would harm Japan economy - LDP.
newsitem.headline: Interest rate change would harm Japan economy - LDP.

text.p: Changing Japan's interest rates, which are currently at record low levels, would undermine the economy, Taku Yamasaki, chairman of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's (LDP) policy research council, said on Monday.
Speaking at the Foreign Correspondents' Club of Japan, Yamasaki said that altering the current record-low level of interest rates would have a negative effect on the economy overall.

"Of course, if the level of interest rates is raised, it may increase consumption by individuals who receive interest income, but overall, I think it is reasonable to think that it (raising rates) would have a negative effect on the economy," Yamasaki said.

Yamasaki also said that it will not be possible to change the level of interest rates without observing the trend of the economy, but added that raising interest rates will become possible once the economy's recovery becomes full-fledged.

"It will not be possible to change interest rates without observing the economy for a while longer...If the economy's recovery becomes full-fledged, raising interest rates will become possible," he said.
Yamasaki said that, in addition to fiscal and monetary policies, the economy can also be stimulated through tax policies.

"I had a discussion with the head of the Finance Ministry's Tax Bureau this morning. I strongly stated (during the discussion) that measures should be taken through taxation policies to stimulate the economy," he said.
Yamasaki added that, from a macro-economic point of view, it will also be necessary to consider drastic steps toward deregulation.
